note: file by atom, read by technique — every entry in Techniques & Templates, keyed by technique id

used_in.implementation: g(p) = 0.5+0.5·cos(2π·|p−c|/pitch) for each grating; the floor keeps a base blue coverage so the field never drops to paper.
used_in.limits: Pitches within ~4 u of each other push the beat fringe past the sheet; equal pitches collapse the moiré to one ring set. Below ~30 u the rings alias into the screen.

used_in.implementation: Multiplying the two gratings gives a dot lattice where both are high and long beat fringes where their phases drift; nothing is drawn as a dot — the lattice is the product.
used_in.limits: knee_lo ≥ knee_hi inverts the smoothstep. gamma below ~0.8 fills the lattice to a flat tint; above ~2.5 the dots shrink to specks.

cutoff.note: red coverage below this prints nothing

used_in.implementation: Red coverage is a clipped gaussian of distance from the core; inside it the blue lattice overprints as a lighter pink, which is how the rings read through the red.
used_in.limits: gain above ~2 saturates the core to a flat disc; sigma above ~700 u floods the sheet and the blue lattice no longer reads through.

params.threshold: uniform random per pixel per ink
params.overprint: where both inks land: overCore pink in the field, overFar plum on lattice dots (product > plum_above) inside the core

used_in.implementation: For each device pixel: blue if r1 < blue_coverage, red if r2 < red_coverage; both → overprint; neither → paper tint. A 0.6 px blur softens the pixel edges the way the reference’s scan does.
used_in.limits: soften above ~1.5 px dissolves the lattice into tone; cell_px is fixed at 1 in this rebuild (a coarser cell needs a hash per cell, not per pixel).

used_in.implementation: Flat cream fill; the print sits inset by 34 u on every side.
used_in.limits: Above ~120 u the margin crops the beat fringe at the left edge.

used_in.implementation: Flat paper fill; the print sits inset on every side.
used_in.limits: Above ~120 u the margin crops the stretched cells at the sheet edge.

params.knockout: each fill clears the same shape on every other plate unless overprinting

used_in.implementation: Every closed shape is filled flat on one plate canvas and cleared from the others (destination-out), so plates only overlap where an overprint is intended.
Each shape is stroked twice on the black plate: 2.2 u on the path, then 1.4 u on the path shifted by a seeded 0.6 u jitter, which thickens the line unevenly.
The shadow side of a shape is clipped and crossed by 45° lines at a 6 u pitch with a 12/4 dash whose phase changes per line; drawn on the black plate so it never slips.
Each color plate is composited with its own down-right offset before the black plate lands in register, so fills open a paper sliver on the top-left of the line and spill past it bottom-right.

Each plate canvas is drawn translated by its own vector; the keyline sits on all three plates, so the offsets show as coloured fringes on every edge and the overprint of all three is the near-black line.
used_in.limits: Past ~8 u a plate leaves its keyline and reads as a second drawing. With all three offsets equal there is no fringe and the print reads as flat digital color.

used_in.implementation: A mid-tone is the plate ink drawn as a regular dot grid clipped to the shape; the dot radius is set from the requested coverage.

params.mottle: perlin fbm 3 oct, cell 120 u, ±3 % multiply

used_in.implementation: Cream flat, then a low-frequency perlin multiply, a 0.35 px blur for the scan, then mono grain over everything including the inks.
One caption centred under each object on the black plate; a sheet title at the top and a folio at the foot.

params.corner_blocks: Archivo 800 condensed caps, 18 u, line 20 u, at (83,55) and (698,55)
params.word_row: JetBrains Mono 700 14 u, seven words justified from 83 u to 922 u at 598 u

used_in.implementation: Plain fills in the caption color; the word row divides the leftover width equally between the words.

params.color: white or pale tint at 0.55–0.72 alpha

used_in.implementation: Three short captions in Inter at 22 u, set flat under the grain so the grain sits on the type too.

params.order: navy 0 · blue 0.10 · cyan 0.22 · white 0.34 · yellow 0.44 · orange 0.54 · pink 0.64 · magenta 0.76 · blue 0.88 · navy 1

used_in.implementation: ART.lut(stops) gives 256 colors; the shading pass indexes it with the environment coordinate t, so color is a function of normal direction only.

normal-shading.name: Normal-buffer shading of a swept slab

params.section: rounded rectangle 300 × 160 u, fillet 30 u, 56 points
params.tilt_rad: 0.5 about the screen x axis through y = 740 u
params.wobble: n += 0.20–0.22·sin/cos fields of period 260–420 u plus 0.06–0.08 at 90–120 u, then normalise

used_in.implementation: Vertices P = C(s) + a·e1 + b·e2 with the section basis rotated by the twist; normals from the cross product of finite differences; triangles rasterized with edge functions into normal + depth buffers; per pixel the reflected ray of the orthographic view picks LUT[t].
band = exp(−((|n.z|−0.34)/0.06)²) mixes the edge color in; spec = (n·h)^60 mixes white in; both read from the same normal buffer as the LUT.

params.multiplicative: ART.grain amp 0.10, pitch 1 px, mono:false, seed 303
params.additive: σ 14/255 per channel on the ground, hashed per pixel, seed 304

used_in.implementation: ART.grain multiplies RGB by 1 + 0.10·n per channel (visible on the chrome and the type); a second pass adds signed noise of 14/255 so the black ground carries grain too, as film does.

params.additive: uniform ±21·(1 − 0.6·L)/255 per pixel, mono, lag-1 correlation 0.25

used_in.implementation: One pass over the whole canvas after every panel is drawn: a mono additive noise scaled down with luminance (it reads in the black, thins in the pink), plus a small per-channel multiplicative term for the color speckle.
Multiplicative hashed noise, identical across channels.

Each word is filled three times in #FF0000, #00FF00, #0000FF with globalCompositeOperation lighter on a transparent layer, offset per channel; where all three overlap the sum is white, at the edges one or two channels show; the layer is drawn under the chrome.

params.small: Archivo 700, 30 u, 2 columns × 3 rows at x 660 / 840, baselines 372 / 402 / 432

used_in.implementation: line 1 is sized to 924 u (font-stretch is set after ctx.font, which resets it); the figure sits on line 2 flush right; the slab is drawn after the type so it covers the bottom of the headline as the reference slab does.

params.css: position: sticky; top: 1.9vw; height: calc(100vh − 1.9vw − 3.4vw); margin: 0 2.4vw 3.4vw

used_in.implementation: Every card is sticky at the same top offset, each a direct child of the scrolling body; the incoming card covers the pinned one, which is clipped at the seam and scaled to 0.95 as it goes under; cards are siblings of one scroll container, not wrapped in sections, so each stays pinned until the end of the page.
Each card is one flat fill; nothing separates cards but the ground showing through the gap and the corner radius.
Fill the sheet, then place six cards on a 3 × 2 grid; the middle column is translated up by 57 u so its cards straddle the row gap.
rrect(24, y, 952, h, 36) filled then used as a clip for everything on the card; the inset panel is a plain rectangle that the clip cuts.

params.border: none on a contrasting ground; 1 u hairline when card ≈ ground
params.clip: all card content is clipped to the rounded path

used_in.implementation: Each card is one rounded-rect path: fill flat, then clip so type can run to the edge and be cut by the corner.

Six tiles, alternately light and dark, each showing one type size: a wide word, a two-line condensed heading, a staggered mono list, a display numeral with mono alphabet rows, cropped display letters, a color-bar table.
Radial gradients on a flat gray, blurred with a 2-D gaussian, then multiplied by mono grain so the gradient does not band.

params.end_cells: bar ends snap to 0.5-pitch cells down the page
params.mask: sum of four text lines, Archivo 900 condensed, blurred 1.2 px

used_in.implementation: For every screen column x_k = k·pitch, walk down the page one device pixel at a time, read the summed letter mask at (x_k + phase, y), map it to a bar width and fill each continuous run as one polygon with a left and a right edge per y.
phase(x,y) = 2.4·fbm(x/260, y/260) plus half a pitch in regions where the field is high; the bar center is x_k + phase, so bars in neighbouring regions step against each other.

params.interior_darken: ink → ink_deep (#3E3A38) where mask > 0.9, ramp from 0.6

used_in.implementation: The bar layer is blurred 0.8 px, its alpha is pushed through a soft threshold so the edge swells outward, and the ink color shifts toward ink_deep inside the letters.
Luminance is multiplied by 1 + mottle before the bars land and by ART.grain after, so ink and paper share one tooth.

params.measured: high-pass std 3.4/255 on paper, 5.5/255 in the core

used_in.implementation: Multiplicative mono grain per device pixel, then a low-frequency perlin mottle, both on the whole sheet including the blobs.
used_in.limits: Grain above ~0.08 reads as noise on the paper and breaks the rim. A mottle cell under ~30 u reads as a second grain.

params.grain: mono, amp 0.05, pitch 1 device px, seed 12

used_in.implementation: Before the perforation punch the stamp layer is multiplied by a low-frequency fbm and then by ART.grain, so both tooth and mottle follow the stamp and stop at the bites.
A mono multiply grain over the finished sheet.
used_in.limits: Above ~0.08 the grain competes with the dots.

used_in.implementation: Each object is a top-face mask drawn in the plane transform; a column scan drops every boundary pixel whose +x or +y probe is empty by the depth, labelling right or left face, top always winning; later objects overwrite earlier ones.
used_in.limits: The drop is a column scan, so a depth past the gap to the object below it paints over that object’s top face. Shapes thinner than 4 px have no interior for the ±2 px probe and get no side faces.

params.yellow: top faces + corner wash + marker strokes

gain.note: yellow corner wash at its center

used_in.implementation: Face labels become three coverage rasters; each raster is coloured mix(white, ink, coverage) on its own canvas and multiplied onto the stock in plate order.
used_in.limits: Keylines past ~8 u close the counters of the letters. The wash is one radial falloff from the lower-left corner; past radius 1.3 it covers the whole sheet and reads as a yellow stock.

used_in.implementation: Before colouring, coverage is multiplied by a blurred copy of itself so fills thin toward their edges, and by a slow perlin mottle; after colouring ART.grain runs mono on the plate and paper pixels are reset to white.
used_in.limits: floor + gain above 1 clips fills to full coverage and the edge thinning disappears. stochastic above ~0.7 breaks the keyline into specks. A mottle scale under ~20 u reads as a second grain, not as uneven inking.

used_in.implementation: Inside the top faces the pink plate is full except where an fbm field crosses zero: the core of the band is paper, the rim half-coverage, which reads as swirls.
used_in.limits: core ≥ rim removes the half-tone rim and the veins go hard-edged. Above scale ~100 u a top face holds less than one vein. One octave gives smooth contour lines, not marble.

params.diagonals: ±30° through the same lattice, 18.2 u apart along a vertical

used_in.implementation: Flat gray fill, then verticals and both diagonal families stroked in the grid ink at 16 % before any plate lands.
used_in.limits: Above alpha ~0.35 the grid competes with the keyline. Under a 14 u pitch the three line families merge into a gray tint.

params.field: Σ (r_i / |p − c_i|_e)⁴, |·|_e an elliptic distance (ratio 1.3–1.6, seeded angle)

used_in.implementation: Sum of inverse-fourth elliptic fields from 10 seeded centres; pixels above 1.0 are white, the rest black, so nearby blobs merge into one shape with a hard edge.

params.fill: radial white → 0.78 gray at the shape edge, union by lighten

used_in.implementation: Four Fourier-radius blobs are filled with a radial white-to-gray gradient on a black canvas (union by lighten) at one-third resolution, blurred with σ = 46 u and read back as a 0..1 luminance field.
used_in.limits: Under σ ~15 u the edge profile is too steep for the ramp and the bands alias. Past σ ~110 u neighboring blobs fuse and the rim stop no longer closes. harmonic_scale above ~2 makes r(θ) cross zero and the outline self-intersects.

used_in.implementation: Six words centred at 225 u (the six-letter word spans 0.92 W), drawn white with globalCompositeOperation difference so each letter inverts the blob field under it.

params.edge: mask padded 40 u so the frame edge does not darken

used_in.implementation: One CSS blur over the full mask after the type is composited, so type edges and blob edges get the same falloff.
256-entry LUT from the stops; every pixel of the blurred mask is replaced by LUT[luminance], which turns the blur falloff into the red-and-pink halo.

params.measured_edge_px: paper→blue 12 · blue→navy 12 · navy 20 · plum→red 25 · red→orange 15 (at 1200 px)

shift.note: slides the field under the ramp

contrast.note: scales the field around 0.5 before the ramp

used_in.implementation: Every pixel of the field is replaced by LUT[field]; the ramp is the only place color enters, so all four colourways share one field.
used_in.limits: The ramp is read at 256 levels; contrast above ~2 leaves fewer than 6 levels across the rim and it stair-steps. A shift past ±0.15 moves the paper stop into the blobs or the core out of range.

used_in.implementation: Each frame recomputes the blobs at quarter scale, composites the cached text mask, blurs at the current σ and gradient-maps on a 512 px work canvas that is drawn up to plate size.

fitted.fit: each word scaled to the card width minus 2 × 14 u

used_in.implementation: Two set sizes: a wrapped all-caps paragraph, and single words each fitted to the inner width and stacked with leading below 0.8 so caps of adjacent lines touch.
Tiny mono rows pinned to the top and bottom edges in two or three columns; a barcode strip is a seeded run of bars with a mono number under it.

params.headline: Archivo 700, 32 u, 4 lines, pitch 37 u, at (340, 322)
params.meta_rows: JetBrains Mono 3.6 u, two rows with boxed keys
params.spine: Archivo 700, 8 u, rotated −90° on both spines
params.marks: 4-point star, globe, QR block, star box

used_in.implementation: All lettering is live type in the three inlined fonts with invented plain words; spine text is drawn on a rotated context.

Where the reference carries a photograph the card fills with a two-stop linear gradient, then five concentric arcs and a disc are stroked in one tint over it; display type sits on top as on the other cards.
A vertical list of event rows: bold title, two or three mono lines, a dotted rule between rows; the ticket row is a boxed strip of five cells with hairline rules and a lozenge stamp under it.
Two 1 u ink rules across the sheet; the caption is set right-aligned 12 u under the first rule, the two-line studio label under the second.
used_in.limits: Rules under 1 device px are drawn at 1 px. A caption past ~22 u collides with the second rule’s label on a narrow sheet.

used_in.implementation: Each panel starts as a canvas linear gradient; C runs from the panel top-left along 66° from horizontal, with knee stops so black holds to 0.15 and pink holds from 0.67.

params.shape: closed spline through 13 measured contour points, off-panel to the left and below
params.halo_strength: four source-over passes of the wide blur: 1 − (1 − h)⁴

used_in.implementation: The shape is drawn twice on padded offscreens: once in crimson and blurred wide (σ 110 u), drawn four times to tint the field; once in black and blurred σ 33 u, drawn over. The wide blur is the halo that reddens the gradient near the black.

params.arc: y = q + (x − cx(q))² / 2R, R 750 u, cx(q) = 217 − 0.8·max(0, q − 233) u (panel-local)
params.right_cut: e fades where x > 333 − 2·max(0, q − 296), over 150 u

used_in.implementation: Per pixel: solve q, the peak height of the arc through the pixel (three fixed-point steps, since the peak x depends on q); darkness = envelope(q) × a thresholded cosine of q whose threshold rises as the envelope falls, so the stripes thin to points where the window cuts off on the right; light stripes sit at the opposite phase. The layer is blurred 3.3 u.

from.note: field value where the dark stop starts

used_in.implementation: The darkest stop sits just under the mid-point of the blurred edge, where the profile is steepest, so it occupies few pixels and reads as a drawn outline; the blue halo is the ramp segment just outside it.
used_in.limits: from must stay below to, and both inside 0.41–0.53 (the stops on either side). A band wider than ~0.07 reads as a dark fill, not an outline.

params.shade: +3 % toward scuff color from v 280 to 580

used_in.implementation: Each panel is a union of rectangles (spine, face, flap, tab, rounded tuck) tested per pixel; the fill is the board color mixed 3 % toward the scuff color by a perlin mottle and a vertical shade, plus sparse one-pixel dots.

params.haze: continuous tint 0.14·exp(−d/3 u) + 0.12·exp(−dc/14 u) + 0.06·exp(−df/2.5 u) under the dots

used_in.implementation: A chamfer distance transform gives d to the silhouette; dc is the distance to the nearest convex corner or fold junction and df to the spine crease or flap fold. A pixel turns lighter where a uniform random is below the summed density times the patch gate, so the wear reads as clustered abrasion rather than a line.
Faint diagonal strokes in the scuff color on a separate layer, blurred 1.5 px, then composited so the edges are soft.

price.tear: jittered polygon, 2 u amplitude on the bottom and right edges

used_in.implementation: Each sticker is a filled path drawn over the worn board with its own drop shadow; the foil is 36 hue wedges on arcs under a radial highlight.

params.digits: JetBrains Mono 3.2 u under the bars

used_in.implementation: A white box, then random-width dark bars from a seeded sequence; the digit row is mono type below the bars.

params.bites: 12 across × 17 down, one centred on each corner

used_in.implementation: The stamp is painted as a rectangle on its own layer, then a circle at every pitch step along all four edges is punched out with destination-out; the punched layer is the clip for everything on the stamp.

Inside the letter mask a dark base is laid first; then a 45° dot lattice is walked and each dot is drawn with radius and color taken from the texture value at its center, so light patches of the texture become large tan dots.

params.font: Archivo 900, wdth 62.5 (extra-condensed; substitute for the reference condensed serif)
params.cap_height_u: ≈ 215 (size fitted so the run is 1003 u)
params.overhang: run ends 40 u above the stamp top

used_in.implementation: The title is drawn once into a mask canvas rotated −90° about its start point; the halftone is composited through it with destination-in, then the result is drawn on the stamp layer under the perforation clip.
Two invented lines centred on a point right of the middle, skewed −12° to stand in for the italic script; drawn after the grain so the white stays clean.

params.project: sc = P / (P − z); sx = cx + x · sc; sy = cy + y · sc
params.order: sort by depth d = (z + R) / 2R, far first

used_in.implementation: 150 particles climb a helix (0.018 of the height per second) while the helix turns (0.22 rad/s); each is projected through a pinhole at 800 u and drawn as text, far to near.

params.no_color_depth: glyphs stay white; only alpha and size carry depth

used_in.implementation: Nothing is shaded: depth is the alpha ramp and the projected font size, so far glyphs are ghosts and near glyphs are ink.
Every glyph with i mod 18 = 7 is replaced by the next palette name, set in its lifted on-ink color at weight 500 with a depth-scaled glow; the animation names its own system.

params.orbit: · with ø every 6th, Ø at center

used_in.implementation: Each animation reads its marks from a short ordered list by index, so the field is typeset from a vocabulary rather than drawn from shapes; the helix list mixes 10 marks with 13 three-digit numbers.
The helix canvas is masked by an elliptical radial gradient so glyphs fade out toward the middle; the title sits in the hole with a wide dark text-shadow that deepens it.

params.input: mx = clientX / innerWidth − 0.5; my = clientY / innerHeight − 0.5

used_in.implementation: The pointer shifts the whole helix by at most 18 u × 14 u, eased at 4 % per frame, so the field drifts after the cursor rather than following it.
A 70 × 8 grid where one sine phase picks both the glyph (from a five-step ramp) and the alpha (by distance to a sine centerline), so a two-wavelength band of laminar glyphs rolls across the frame.
Eighteen glyphs along a line lit by the positive half of one travelling sine, so a soft blue pulse runs left to right behind a fixed ▸ head; it lives inline under a dialogue turn.
52 glyphs on a flattened ellipse, each with its own breathing radius and an alpha that peaks at the bottom of the orbit; the canvas is held at 30 % under a pull quote.

params.reduced_motion: draw once at t = now, no loop

used_in.implementation: One setupCanvas and one loop helper serve all four canvases; under prefers-reduced-motion the loop degenerates to a single still frame, so the page keeps its picture without motion.

params.source: Planck 3000 K, green dip .1 at 548 ± 48 nm
params.integration: 380–720 nm, 4 nm steps, Wyman–Sloan–Shirley CMF fit

used_in.implementation: For every δ from 0 to 1599 nm the transmitted spectrum sin²(πδ/λ)·S(λ) is integrated against the color-matching functions; the 1600 colors are the LUT the field is shaded with. Order 1 (0–560 nm) is where the plates live: black → grey → warm white → amber → orange → red; the mauve and blue of 560–700 are the cool lanes.

params.sheet: δ = (d0 + A · sign(c)|c|^shape) · (1 + pin/r), c = cos(k · θw + ph + flow · t); shape for the peaks (blue), shapeN for the dips (pale) — the pale lanes are the narrow ones
params.radial: + rad · r — orange near the focus, red far out
params.load: δ = K · |σ1 − σ2| from Σ Flamant point loads (σr = −2F cos(θ−α)/(π r^decay)) + a uniform stress
params.biaxial: δ = d0 + c · |p − A| · |p − B| (Cassini ovals)
params.ribbon: δ = d0 + A · tanh(d / period) — a ramp across the ribbon: white, orange, red, blue in order
params.ring: δ = d0 + A · tanh((r − R) / period)

used_in.implementation: Each family is one expression for δ. The sheet keeps δ in the orange-red most of the time (shape 2.4 dwells near d0) and dips to white or peaks to blue briefly; the load family is real plane-stress mechanics; the conoscopes are the textbook interference figures.

params.domain_warp: (x, y) += wa · noise2((x, y) · wf), 2-octave value noise, wa .1 W, wf 1.2; the same hash in JS and GLSL
params.sheet: ψ = θw + twist · r + spiral · ln r
params.load: ψ = ½ · atan2(2τ, σx − σy) (principal direction)

used_in.implementation: ψ decides where the isoclinics fall. The domain warp bends the sheet — the plates are not flat starbursts — and warping θ makes lanes of unequal width; neither breaks the physics because δ and ψ are still evaluated from one coordinate.

params.term: sin²(m · (ψ − β + skew · sin(ψ − β)))^sharp, sharp for the β arm and sharp2 for the β + 180° arm
params.circular: circ mixes toward 1 (a circular polariscope removes isoclinics)
params.note: m = 2 is the physical crossed-polar cross (four arms); the plates read as two arms, m = 1, one polarizer effective

used_in.implementation: Multiplies the whole image; the black wedges are not masks but extinction where the material axis is parallel to the polarizer. Spinning β sweeps them around the focus.
mix(floor, chart(δ) · iso, env): the load point is opaque, the far field sinks, nothing reaches 0.

params.hue_grade: after gamma, hues pulled .75 of the way toward 6° (warm) or 196° (cool), whichever is nearer; saturation × 1.4 first
params.bloom: highlights (brightness .8, contrast 2.5 → a threshold near L .4) blurred at σ .05 W and added at .4 — the glow along the hot edges
params.shoulder: x/(1 + .25x), then highlights above L .6 desaturate .85 toward a pink-white
params.measured: plates carry no yellow, no green, no magenta — the grade explains the absence; band means: (235,182,147) (232,143,94) (225,95,57) (185,53,40) red side, (165,196,199) (120,154,165) (79,105,116) blue side, white (222,190,184)

used_in.implementation: Applied to the chart once (1600 entries), so per-pixel cost is a lookup; this is the step that turns a textbook chart into the plate palette.

params.measured: p99 horizontal gradient 12/255 per px at 1600 px

used_in.implementation: One gaussian over the finished color image; blurring after the chart is what mixes neighboring lanes into the grey-mauve transitions.
Every motion is a physical control of the instrument: rotate the polarizer, load the sheet, turn the sheet.

params.subject: headland with a signal tower and sheds, sea, far ridge — generated, lit from the left

res.note: source resolution as a fraction of the sheet

used_in.implementation: Sky, ridge, headland and sea are evaluated per pixel from seeded Perlin noise; tower, sheds and boat are drawn as flat lit/shadow faces on top. The function returns a canvas; every later technique only reads it.
used_in.limits: Any RGB picture works in its place. Pictures with no smooth area above upper_v show no guilloche; pictures with no pixel inside the hue range print as one ink.

used_in.implementation: Luminance is exposed and stretched about mid-gray before it sets any line width, so paper and solid shadow are reached inside the picture, not only at its extremes.
used_in.limits: Contrast above ~2 clips most of the sheet to paper or solid line; the swelling line then reads as a two-level threshold.

amp_pitches.note: phase shift in pitches at flow = 1 for a black-to-white step

used_in.implementation: A quarter-resolution copy of the picture is blurred; its luminance is added to the line phase, so lines rise over light forms and sink into dark ones. The same pass stores blurred edge energy for the guilloche mask.
used_in.limits: flow · amp_pitches · pitch must stay under ~1.5 × radius or neighboring lines fold over each other at hard edges.

pitch_u.note: reference: 3.2 px on its own image; 6 u resolves at plate size

used_in.implementation: Distance to the nearest line center is compared with half the tone-set width and antialiased over one device pixel. In the highlights each line is cut into dashes whose fill falls with darkness, with a hashed offset per line.
used_in.limits: Under ~2.5 device px of pitch the lines alias into tone. duty_max · weight at 1 closes the shadows to solid ink and the crosshatch has nothing to cross.

used_in.implementation: A second, unwarped line set whose width ramps from 0 at start to duty_max · strength at full darkness; the two sets are combined as 1 − (1−a)(1−b).
used_in.limits: start under ~0.35 puts hatch into the midtones and the picture reads as a net, not an engraving.

curvature.note: max slope of the wave; amplitude = curvature · scale / 2π

tone.note: how much darkness thickens the guilloche line

drift.note: phase wander of family A down the sheet

shear.note: family B phase advance per unit y, in units of 2π/S — tilts the braid so it does not stripe

params.lines: A: y + a·sin(2πx/S + drift·sin(2πy/2.3S)) = k·pitch;  B: y − a·sin(2πx/S + shear·2πy/S + 1.1) = k·pitch

used_in.implementation: Two families of stacked sine lines, mirrored, give the braided cells. Vertical distance is divided by √(1 + slope²) so line width stays even on the steep parts. The mask is (above upper_v) × (edge energy low); the straight lines fade by the same mask.
used_in.limits: curvature above ~3 makes the wave steeper than the antialiasing estimate holds; pitch near the main pitch makes the hand-over at upper_v invisible.

hue-key.name: Kept hue as a second ink

params.mode: variant.accent — "hue": ink takes each pixel’s own hue · "#hex": one custom ink · "off": monochrome

used_in.implementation: Mask = 1 inside tolerance of the chosen hue, feathered to 0, gated by saturation, scaled by strength and pulled back toward the main ink in the shadows by keep_shadows. It changes ink color only — line width is unchanged.
used_in.limits: tolerance + feather above ~90° keys most warm pictures whole; min_sat under ~8 % keys neutral grays by their noise hue.

used_in.implementation: One multiplicative monochrome noise pass over paper and ink together, on cells of 1.4 u with lag-1 correlation.
used_in.limits: Above ~0.06 the grain reads before the line; this pass is the last thing to add and the first to remove.

spacing.note: lobe centers sit this many radii apart

used_in.implementation: Each bank is a row of circles along a spine from one point to another, filled together with the polygon under the spine; later banks cover earlier ones.
used_in.limits: spacing above ~1.9 opens gaps between lobes and the edge reads as beads. R_var above ~0.6 makes single lobes swallow their neighbors.

params.tone: one dot color per fill, close to the fill; the sky carries no dot layer

used_in.implementation: One dot per grid cell, moved by up to 0.42 of the pitch; the fill under the dot center picks the dot color.
used_in.limits: radius above ~0.45 × pitch merges dots into a tint. jitter 0 shows the grid as rows. Below 3.5 u pitch the layer costs over 100 k dots per sheet.

used_in.implementation: A two-octave noise field gives each dot a keep probability between the floor and 1.
used_in.limits: floor at 1 removes the shading. scale under ~80 u reads as blotches, not form.

gap_u.note: no two dots closer than this

used_in.implementation: Dots are placed along each ray with a spread that narrows to the tip and a count that thins with distance; a gaussian core sits on the center. A dot is dropped when another already sits within the gap. Dots land only on the sky.
used_in.limits: Over ~60 rays the streams merge into a disc; root_width above ~140 u does the same. core_dots at 0 leaves the rays unjoined. gap at 0 lets dots pile up and the burst reads as spray, not stipple.

params.q: c + d / (1 + k·|d/R|²), with d.y scaled by 1 − stretch_y·clamp(−d.y/R, 0, 1)·0.5

used_in.implementation: Each pixel is mapped to a sample point pulled toward the lens center by 1/(1 + k·r²); the grid is evaluated at the sample point.
used_in.limits: k below about −0.6 folds the grid over itself inside the sheet. k above ~3 stretches the outer cells past the sheet and they read as bars.

grow.note: added width at full field strength

edge.note: softness of a band edge, in cell units

share.note: share of cells that carry it

cell_var.note: how much ring strength varies cell to cell

used_in.implementation: Inside each cell the distance to the center is measured as a superellipse; two bands of that distance carry ink and the space past 0.45 carries a lighter tint. Both strengthen with a gaussian field centered on the lens.
used_in.limits: outer.at + width + grow above ~0.6 closes every gutter and the cells read as holes in a flat tint. Pitch under ~28 u falls below the speckle and the rings vanish.

mix.note: chance that a cell takes its second-nearest ink

params.inner: the inner ring takes the next ink in the list

used_in.implementation: Five anchor points carry one ink each. A cell takes the ink of its nearest anchor, or with up to 30 % chance the second nearest.
used_in.limits: sharpness under ~1.5 mixes every region and no ink dominates anywhere. mix above ~0.4 reads as random color.

stray.note: share of stock pixels that take an ink

used_in.implementation: Per pixel: ink if a random number is under the coverage, else stock; a share of stock pixels take a random ink. A 0.8 px blur follows.
used_in.limits: stray above ~0.2 lifts the stock to a tint and the rings lose contrast. soften above ~1.5 px turns the speckle into tone.

used_in.implementation: Each meridian is an ellipse with the sphere radius as its tall axis and radius·|sin λ| as its wide one, stroked with a 6 on 5 dash.
used_in.limits: Over ~31 meridians the dashes of neighbors align into bands. A radius under the half-height of the sheet shows the sphere outline and the picture reads as a ball, not a field.

fan_u.note: length of the line the strokes end along

stagger.note: share of the reach by which stroke ends step back across the bundle

params.curve: quadratic; control point at mid-chord, pushed sideways by bend × chord length

used_in.implementation: For each bundle a target point is picked around the hub; stroke ends are spaced along a line through it, and each stroke is a quadratic curve whose sideways bend steps up across the bundle.
used_in.limits: fan under ~10 u collapses a bundle to one thick line. Past ~24 bundles the sheet fills and single arcs stop reading.

params.ink_step: ink index steps across the bundle, mixed with the next ink

used_in.implementation: A linear gradient from the hub to the stroke end colors each stroke: faint at the root, full ink at the tip. Strokes are composited with the lighter blend.
used_in.limits: With both alphas at 1 on a dark ground, crossings near the hub clip to white.

used_in.implementation: The stroke layer is blurred and added back over itself.
used_in.limits: gain above ~1 washes the thin strokes into a haze.

used_in.implementation: Square markers sit on bundle ends and on seeded free points; each carries a seeded number set up and to the right.
used_in.limits: Over ~60 nodes the labels overlap. Type under 9 u is unreadable at 900 px.
